'''John Stuart Foster Jr.''' (September 18, 1922 – April 25, 2025) was an American physicist, best known as the fourth director of [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]] and as [[Director, Defense Research and Engineering]] under four Secretaries of Defense and two Presidents.

==Early life and education==
Foster was born September 18, 1922, in [[New Haven, Connecticut]]. He received his [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in 1948 from [[McGill University]], where his father, Canadian physicist [[John Stuart Foster|John S. Foster, Sr.]], was a faculty member. He received his bachelor's from [[McGill University]] in 1948 and his doctorate in physics from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1952, while serving as a staff member of the university's [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]] in California.<ref>https://www.washingtonpost.com/obituaries/2025/05/07/john-foster-dead-nuclear-physics/</ref><ref name="CCST">{{Cite web |title=John S. Foster, Jr. |url=https://ccst.us/people/senior-fellows/john-s-foster-jr/ |access-date=2025-04-30 |website=California Council on Science & Technology (CCST) |language=en-US}}</ref> In 1979, he received an honorary Doctor of Science from the [[University of Missouri]].

==Early career==
During [[World War II]], before he received his bachelor's degree, Foster began his career in the [[Radio Research Laboratory (Harvard)|Radio Research Laboratory]] at [[Harvard University]]. He was an advisor to the [[Fifteenth Air Force|15th Air Force]] on radar and radar countermeasures in the [[Mediterranean Theater of Operations, United States Army|Mediterranean Theater of Operations]] in 1943 and 1944. In the summers of 1946 and 1947, he worked on the [[Chalk River Laboratories|Canadian nuclear power project]] in [[Chalk River|Chalk River, Ontario]].<ref name="CCST"/>

==Lawrence Livermore Laboratory==
In 1952, Foster was recruited to [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory|Lawrence Livermore Laboratory]] by its founder [[Edward Teller]], and became a division leader in experimental physics. He was promoted to associate director in 1958, and director of the Livermore Laboratory and associate director of the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory in 1961, in which positions he served until 1965.<ref name="CCST"/>

[[File:FosterLaird600.jpg|left|thumb|Foster with Secretary of Defense [[Melvin Laird]], 1972]]

==Department of Defense==
Foster was appointed director of defense research and engineering, a position then considered the number-three job in the [[United States Department of Defense|Department of Defense]], by Secretary of Defense [[Robert S. McNamara]] in October 1965. He continued in this position until June 1973, serving under Presidents [[Lyndon B. Johnson]] and [[Richard Nixon]], and under Secretaries of Defense McNamara, [[Clark Clifford]], [[Melvin Laird]], and [[Elliot Richardson]].<ref name="LBJ">{{Cite web |last=Library |first=LBJ |title=John S. Foster, Jr. Oral Histories: LBJ Library |url=http://www.lbjlib.utexas.edu/johnson/archives.hom/oralhistory.hom/Foster-J/Foster-J.asp |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160519185605/http://www.lbjlib.utexas.edu:80/johnson/archives.hom/oralhistory.hom/Foster-J/Foster-J.asp |archive-date=2016-05-19 |access-date=2025-04-30 |website=www.lbjlib.utexas.edu}}</ref>

==Later career==
From 1973, Foster was vice president, science and technology of [[TRW Inc.|TRW]], retiring in 1988. He continued to serve on the board of directors of TRW from 1988 to 1994. He was a Consultant to [[Northrop Grumman]], Ninesigma, [[G4S Secure Solutions|Wackenhut Services, Inc.]], and Defense Group, Inc. He was also chairman of the Board of Pilkington Aerospace, Inc., and Chairman of Technology Strategies and Alliances.

From 1973 until 1990, he was a member of the [[President's Foreign Intelligence Advisory Board]]. He was a long-serving member of the [[Defense Science Board]], of which he served as chairman from January 1990 to June 1993.<ref name="CCST"/>

==Later life and death==
Foster [[Centenarian|turned 100]] on September 18, 2022. He continued to advise and mentor scientists at Livermore into the 2020s.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bishop |first1=Breanna |last2=Chen |first2=Allan |url=https://www.llnl.gov/article/48996/johnny-foster-100 |title=Johnny Foster at 100 |work=[[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]] |date=September 15, 2022 |access-date=November 26, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://livermorelabfoundation.org/2023/04/25/john-s-foster-undergrad-fellowship/ |title=LF Announces Fellowship in honor of Dr. John S. Foster Jr., LLNL's Fourth Director |work=[[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory|Livermore Lab Foundation]] |date=April 25, 2023 |access-date=January 16, 2024}}</ref> He died from heart failure in [[Santa Barbara, California]], on April 25, 2025, at the age of 102.<ref>{{Cite web |title=John Foster Jr. Obituary − Santa Barbara, CA |url=https://neptunesociety.com/obituaries/santa-barbara-ca/john-foster-jr-12354372 |access-date=2025-04-30 |website=Neptune Cremation Service |language=en-us}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=John S. Foster Jr., Pentagon scientist who developed warheads, dies at 102|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/obituaries/2025/05/07/john-foster-dead-nuclear-physics/|last=Smith|first=Harrison|publisher=The Washington Post|date=May 7, 2025|access-date=May 7, 2025}}</ref>

==Public positions==
Foster's public positions have consistently reflected his support of a robust [[Nuclear weapons of the United States|U.S. nuclear stockpile]].<ref name="IPS">{{Cite web |title=John Foster Jr. |url=https://militarist-monitor.org/profile/john-foster-jr/ |access-date=2025-04-30 |website=Militarist Monitor |language=English}}</ref><ref>John S. Foster Jr. and Keith B. Payne, [http://www.aps.org/units/fps/newsletters/2007/october/foster-payne.html "What Are Nuclear Weapons For?"], American Physical Society Forum on Physics and Society, vol. 36, no. 4 (October 2007)</ref>

During the [[Presidency of George W. Bush|George W. Bush administration]], Foster was a prominent advocate for a return to nuclear testing and for the design of a new generation of U.S. nuclear weapons. He chaired the "Panel to Assess the Reliability, Safety, and Security of the United States Nuclear Stockpile," created in 1998 by [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] Sen. [[Jon Kyl]] of [[Arizona]], a longtime foe of the [[Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty]]. The panel, popularly known as the "Foster Panel", issued several reports advocating increased weapons spending.<ref name="IPS"/><ref>Stephen Schwartz, "The New-Nuke Chorus Tunes Up," Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists, July/August 2001</ref><ref>Philipp C. Bleek, [http://www.armscontrol.org/act/2002_04/fosterapril02 "Foster Panel Calls for Reducing Nuclear Test Preparation Time"], Arms Control Today, April 2002</ref>

Foster was a prominent member of the commission to Assess the Threat to the United States from Electromagnetic Pulse ([[Electromagnetic pulse|EMP]]) Attack, established by the 2001 Defense Authorization Act. The commission's report called for strong defensive measures across a wide range of industries and public services.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-28 |title=Homepage |url=http://www.empcommission.org |access-date=2025-04-30 |website=EMPCommission.org |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
Foster received the Founder's Award from the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 1989, and the [[Enrico Fermi Award]] in 1992. His other awards include the [[Ernest Orlando Lawrence Award]] of the [[United States Atomic Energy Commission|Atomic Energy Commission]] (1960), the [[Department of Defense Medal for Distinguished Public Service|Defense Department's Distinguished Public Service Medals]] (1969, 1973, 1993), election to the National Academy of Engineering (1969), the James Forrestal Memorial Award (1969), the H.H. Arnold Trophy (1971), the Crowell Medal (1972), the WEMA Award (1973), and the [[Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany|Knight Commander's Cross (Badge and Star) of the Order of Merit]] of the [[Germany|Federal Republic of Germany]] (1974). Foster was a commander, [[Legion of Honor]], [[France|Republic of France]].<ref name="CCST"/>
